legal_basis.from: Confirmed via three independent contemporaneous news reports (WPSU, The Courier-Express/Jeffersonian Democrat, and explorejeffersonpa.com/EYT) that the moratorium was adopted as a Borough Council motion -- made by Second Vice-President Randy Bartley during the property committee's report at the June 16, 2026 regular meeting -- rather than as a separately numbered ordinance or resolution. The Courier-Express: 'The moratorium was approved during a report by the property committee regarding some rezoning in the borough. The motion was made by Randy Bartley... The motion passed unanimously.' No ordinance or resolution number exists for this action because it was adopted by motion.
legal_basis.to: Borough Council reportedly adopted a 180-day data-center moratorium by motion on June 16, 2026. The official instrument and minutes have not been located; whether a separate numbered instrument exists is unresolved.
legal_basis.reason: Contemporaneous reporting supports a council vote but does not establish that no numbered instrument exists.

current_status.from: Active as of 2026-09-23, running toward its computed 180-day expiry (~2026-12-13/14). Adopted by unanimous Borough Council motion on 2026-06-16, pausing data center development in the borough and barring data centers from using Brookville's municipal water system (which also serves Corsica, Pinecreek Elementary School, and the Jefferson County Fairgrounds outside the borough). The action was prompted by unofficial word of two possible nearby data center projects -- one in Pine Creek Township, one in Rose Township -- that officials estimated could together require about 2.4 million gallons of water per day; no formal application had been filed for either as of adoption. No news of an extension, permanent ordinance, or repeal was found in sources reviewed through 2026-09-23.
current_status.to: June 24 WPSU reporting describes a unanimous Council vote for a 180-day data-center pause. Original minutes and any separate numbered instrument remain unlocated; a reported motion does not prove no such instrument exists. Actual effective interval and later action remain unresolved. current_status.from: Active as of 2026-09-23; the moratorium's precise end date is not independently confirmed (estimated late October 2026 from a six-month term starting April 30, 2026). Since adoption, Linde Corporation's application (submitted the same day as the moratorium) proceeded through contested public hearings, including a May 7, 2026 planning commission session drawing roughly 250 attendees. On 2026-09-14, the Board of Supervisors -- following a unanimous Planning Commission recommendation to deny -- unanimously rejected Linde's preliminary land development plan for 20 data center buildings and two gas-fired power plants, finding it did not meet the township's Subdivision and Land Development Ordinance (insufficient detail on environmental protections, stormwater management, and infrastructure impacts). Linde is widely expected to appeal to Wayne County Court. [VERIFY instrument number; primary source (news-only evidence) not confirmed at confidence 0.65 in the 2026-09 refresh]
